subject.title: WhatsApp inter_session delivery requests can be wrongly suppressed as REPLY_SKIP / ANNOUNCE_SKIP / NO_REPLY

question: Should this WhatsApp explicit-delivery symptom be fixed by narrowing and landing the current requester-return-path PR, or by waiting for the broader structured sessions_send delivery-intent contract?
rationale: The remaining work changes model-facing A2A delivery semantics and overlaps an open structured handoff issue, so automation should not choose the permanent prompt/protocol direction alone.

options.title: Repair And Land Narrow PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311 as the concrete fix after preserving prompt-cache guardrails, redacting identifiers, and adding/confirming WhatsApp or equivalent source-reply proof.

options.title: Fold Into Structured Handoff
options.body: Keep this issue open until the broader handoff contract explicitly covers delivery intent, skip/no-reply outcomes, and channel/thread inheritance.

options.title: Wait For Fresh Live Repro
options.body: Keep current code unchanged until maintainers have a current live WhatsApp proof that distinguishes this symptom from legitimate `NO_REPLY` suppression.

recommendation.title: Repair And Land Narrow PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311 as the concrete fix after preserving prompt-cache guardrails, redacting identifiers, and adding/confirming WhatsApp or equivalent source-reply proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from sessions_send feature history and related handoff triage direction.
